answer: Anyone can insure an identity against clonehood at a market rate, and when the identity is proved to be a clone the insurer pays out of its own reserve, which turns detection into a revenue stream for whoever performs it. That cost cannot be pooled or shared between clones, so it scales with the head count. The zenith is the premium, the onyx the underwriting pool that pays on a clone proof, and the spiral the correlated funding that sets the price; the zenith scales with the spiral, and the onyx only pays when the clone is actually proved.
